integration_effects.composed_bff_path: COHERENT. apps/api/src/middleware/app-auth.ts builds hubAuthConfig = tryLoadHubAuthConfig(hubEnvBag(env)) at module scope, then maps hubAuthConfig.clientId -> HubSdkConfig.publishableKey and hubAuthConfig.clientSecret -> secretKey with an explicit comment that 1.3.1 still names them so and sends them as client_id/client_secret. audience is ALWAYS passed, so the SDK's own derivation is never consulted. createAppAuthBff recomputes hubEnvBag(env) once and feeds all three redirect resolvers from it.
integration_effects.encryption_ikm: RESOLVES CORRECTLY. encryptionIkm: env.HUB_SESSION_ENCRYPTION_KEY ?? hubAuthConfig.clientSecret. clientSecret is the renamed carrier of the same Hub client secret the retired FXL_HUB_SECRET_KEY held, so the HKDF input is unchanged in VALUE. env.ts emptyToUndefined still turns a blank override into undefined so the documented default applies. session-crypto.ts header updated to name FXL_HUB_CLIENT_SECRET. integration_effects.read_beside_get: HOLDS. hub-session-store.ts declares read(): Promise<HubSessionReadResult> on the transaction handle and implements get() as a PROJECTION of the same resolved outcome object (const read = async () => outcome; get() awaits read()), never a second lookup, so 1.3.1's BFF still calls a get() that exists and the two accessors cannot drift. The 169-test RLS/integration suite that drives the real Postgres store passes.
integration_effects.discriminated_union_narrowing: HOLDS. createHubSessionStore still returns {kind:'durable'; store: DurableHubSessionStore} | {kind:'memory'; store: EphemeralHubSessionStore}, and app-auth.ts mounts createHubLoginSupersedeMiddleware only under if (session.kind === 'durable'). The class-level kind = 'persistent' / 'ephemeral' properties added by slice 01 are a SEPARATE forward-compatibility surface for the 2.x store contract and do not collide with the factory's durable/memory discriminator; type-check exit 0 confirms the narrowing still compiles.

findings.detail: encryptionIkm now derives from hubAuthConfig.clientSecret (FXL_HUB_CLIENT_SECRET) where it previously derived from FXL_HUB_SECRET_KEY. The value is the same Hub client secret, so seals keep opening PROVIDED the deploy copies the value across under the new name. If a deploy sets a different value, every stored session invalidates and every user re-logs in once. Code is correct; this is a promotion checklist item.

summary: PASS. All five gate commands exit 0 on integrated master. Suite is 1298 tests (80 shared-utils, 448 api, 770 web), up 33 from the 1265 baseline with the entire rise in apps/api and no package falling; the API integration suite is separately green at 169 tests over the local Docker database, with setup-env.ts's hard DATABASE_URL override confirmed still in force. The two slices compose coherently: app-auth.ts reads hubEnvBag(env), maps clientId/clientSecret onto 1.3.1's publishableKey/secretKey and always passes the configured audience, encryptionIkm resolves to hubAuthConfig.clientSecret with the blank-override guard intact, slice 01's read() sits beside a get() that is a pure projection of the same outcome so the installed BFF still finds it, and the durable/memory discriminated union still narrows the /auth/callback login-supersede mount. The integration-level non-vacuity probe went red exactly as on slice 02's branch (4 failed of 12, the named oracle among them) and was restored to a byte-identical working tree. Nothing fails open: the 503 unconfigured path, the 401 missing-context path and the 402 entitlement gate are all unchanged, and every malformed configuration now throws at boot rather than degrading. No credential is in a tracked file, no secret is logged or interpolated into an error, and the retired publishable-key literal survives only in slice 04's web env examples, the two CLAUDE.md lines, one deliberate negative test fixture and historical nexo documents. House rules clean. One carried, non-blocking finding confirmed and left for slice 03 step 10b as planned.
